articles.title: Libres 1 F1 del GP de Azerbaiyán: resumen, resultado y tiempos de Alonso y Sainz en Bakú
articles.summary: Cerramos por el momento pero... no os vayáis muy lejos que enseguida volvemos con los Libres 2 del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán, los cuales darán comienz
articles.body:
Última hora de los libres de Fórmula 1 del GP de Azerbaiyán, en directo:

Comienza el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán en Bakú. Tras haber estrenado el Madring hace ya un par de semanas, arranca la última prueba europea de la temporada, con un Mundial muy encaminado hacia el joven piloto italiano, Kimi Antonelli.

El piloto de Mercedes ha ganado las dos últimas pruebas tras el regreso del parón de verano, en Monza y Madring , sumando así su octava victoria de las 14 pruebas disputadas . Esto ha conllevado que que Kimi sume un total de 292 puntos , 81 por encima de su compañero de equipo, George Russell , y 101 sobre Lewis Hamilton . Ambos británicos han empezado a dar por perdido el Mundial debido a las azañas del de Mercedes y su incapacidad a hacerle frente.

Mientras Red Bull y McLaren parecen haber dado con la tecla para tratar de empezar a luchar por mayores posiciones, tal y como ya sucedió en el Gran Premio de España , donde Lando Norris consiguó la primera Pole en el Madring , la cual podría haber acabado en victoria de no ser por un error en la parada, y Max Verstappen , quien finalmente se acabó subiendo al segundo escalón del pódium, justo por delante del británico.

Los españoles, por el contrario, siguen sufriendo más de lo que les gustaría. Ambos padecieron bastantes dificultades durante el Gran Premio de casa, el cual terminó en un 17º puesto por parte de Fernando Alonso , a pesar de las mejoras, y un DNF por parte de Carlos Sainz . No obstante, este fin de semana parece ser que el madrileño dispondrá de un coche "prácticamente nuevo ", tal y como ha declarado James Vowels, Jefe de Equipo de Williams .

Isack Hadjar regresa a la competición tras tres Grandes Premios de baja a causa de su lesión en la muñeca izquierda, la cuál está completamente recuperada, o lo suficiente para pilotar, tal y como el mismo piloto ha declarado. Además, ayer mismo se anunció la renovación del francés el Red Bull Racing , gracis a sus buenas actuciones, tal y como se ha trasladado desde el equipo.

articles.title: Horarios del GP de Azerbaiyán de F1: fechas y dónde ver en TV la carrera de Sainz y Alonso en Bakú
articles.standfirst: Con el Mundial encarando ya la recta final de esta loca temporada, el urbano de Bakú es el escenario del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán... que tiene horarios diferentes a lo habitual
articles.summary: Con el Mundial encarando ya la recta final de esta loca temporada, el urbano de Bakú es el escenario del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán... que tiene horarios diferentes a lo habitual
articles.body: Tras un fin de semana de descanso tras el Gran Premio de España, la Fórmula 1 vuelve por todo lo alto con el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán. Después del estreno de Madring, el campeonato repite en un urbano de última generación como es el circuito de Bakú. Pese a que Madrid proponía una pista nueva para todos... acabó pasando lo de casi siempre: Kimi volvió a ganar. El joven piloto italiano sumó su octava victoria de la temporada aventajando ya en 81 puntos a su compañero de equipo, George Russell, quien empieza a descartarse para el Mundial, tras firmar un 5º puesto en Madring. En el pódium le acompañaron Max Verstappen, quien supo sacar el máximo rendimiento a su Red Bull y aprovecharlo para firmar un 2º puesto. Lando Norris también subió al pódium de Madring, aunque no como le hubiera gustado. El piloto inglés firmó la primera pole en el circuito español, pero un error de su equipo durante la parada en boxes le arrebató una victoria más que segura. Los españoles por otro lado siguen sufriendo. Fernando Alonso y Carlos Sainz no pudieron hacer nada para revertir su situación en el Gran Premio de casa y ambos pilotos acabaron en muy malas posiciones: Carlos sin terminar y Fernando, 17º. Aún y así, los españoles acabaron más que agradecidos con su público, los cuales siguieron apoyándolos a pesar de las circunstancias. Mientras Lewis Hamilton, al igual que Russell, cada vez tiene más complicadas sus opciones de campeonato tras su abandono en Madring que le aleja ya a 101 puntos del italiano. La gran duda de cara al GP de Azerbaiyán recae en el posible regreso de Isack Hadjar, quien sigue siendo baja debido a su lesión en la muñeca. Red Bull no quiere precipitar su regreso provocándole una recaída aún peor que la propia lesión por lo que, a no ser que se encuentre al 100%, el francés seguirá siendo sustituido por Lawson y éste, a su vez, por Yuki Tsunoda. Definitivamente, el tema estrella a lo largo de estas dos semanas desde el final de Madring ha sido el futuro de Fernando Alonso. El piloto asturiano aún no ha dado ninguna declaración con respecto a si seguirá o no en la F1 a partir de la próxima temporada, tan solo se ha dedicado a jugar y especular sobre lo que podrá suceder, mientras que Aston Martin y el campeonato hacen todo lo posible para que el español continúe conduciendo un F1. Atentos a esta carrera porque hay un importante cambio respecto al planning habitual. Y es que la carrera del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán se disputará... en sábado (y con un horario también diferente, con el semáforo verde previsto para las 13:00 horas). Y eso significa que todo el programa se adelanta un día, con los libres arrancando el jueves y la clasificación el viernes. Como es habitual, el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán de Fórmula 1 2026 se podrá ver en directo por televisión a través de DAZN F1 y en Movistar +. También tienes la opción de seguir todo lo que suceda en la carrera en el circuito de Bakú a través de los directos de MARCA.com y la transmisión de la carrera en Radio MARCA. JUEVES 24 DE SEPTIEMBRE Entrenamientos Libres 1: 10:30 horas - 11:30 horas. Entrenamientos Libres 2: 14:00 horas - 15:00 horas. VIERNES 25 DE SEPTIEMBRE Entrenamientos Libres 3: 10:30 horas - 11:30 horas. Clasificación del GP de Bakú: 14:00 horas. SABADO 26 DE SEPTIEMBRE Carrera del GP de Bakú (51 vueltas): 13:00 horas.

articles.title: ¡Fuego en los frenos del mejorado Williams de Carlos Sainz!
articles.standfirst: El madrileño sólo había completado cinco vueltas y su FW48 sufrió problemas para empezar el fin de semana en Bakú
articles.summary: El madrileño sólo había completado cinco vueltas y su FW48 sufrió problemas para empezar el fin de semana en Bakú
articles.body: El fin de semana que se suponía que cambiaría la dinámica de Williams en términos de rendimiento con su mayor mejora de la temporada no empezó como debería. El FW48 de Carlos Sainz, claro jefe de filas desde que aterrizó en la estructura británica, perdió parte de su trabajo del viernes de libres tras sufrir problemas en los primeros compases del Libre 1. Sólo había completado cinco vueltas cuando sus frenos dijeron basta y obligaron al parón del piloto madrileño en el inicio de su programa de trabajo. La imagen es del todo espectacular. Sainz entró en boxes tras cinco vueltas y ya desde que circulaba por el pit-lane sacó el brazo para avisar a sus mecánicos. Rápidamente, desde la radio le lanzaron el aviso: "Apaga el coche. Los frenos están en llamas". Y cuando la cámara enfocó al tren trasero, no existieron dudas. El fuego salía al exterior. No es la mejor noticia para un Williams que viene con cinco mejoras declaradas ante la FIA, con los conductos de freno, tanto delanteros como traseros, más trabajados respecto a los que iniciaron el año. Todavía falta por aclararse si el motivo de los problemas viene dado por algo surgido de la novedad o es una causa ajena como exceso de temperatura y objetos externos. Dentro de lo malo, Williams sólo perdió 17 minutos por los problemas de Sainz con los frenos. El equipo británico le devolvió a pista cuando los primeros neumáticos blandos del libre hicieron aparición. No es nada excesivamente dramático y podrá seguir trabajando con el nuevo paquete del FW48. En total, son cinco grandes novedades que buscarán revivir a un coche que sólo ha sumado 11 puntos (6 de Sainz y 5 de Albon) en la primera parte de esta temporada. Eso sí, en ningún momento ha adelantado que cambiará radicalmente su rendimiento. "No es de un segundo y medio, nos seguirá costando salir de Q1 y pelear en Q2. Habrá circuitos, como Austin o Malasia, donde volveremos a sufrir", relató. Aunque la cosa no se parecerá a un Madring que señalaban como el peor fin de semana posible.

articles.title: Azerbaijan Grand Prix: George Russell fastest as Kimi Antonelli stops on track with hydraulic leak
articles.summary: Mercedes driver George Russell heads Red Bull's Max Verstappen in first practice at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Mercedes driver George Russell headed Red Bull's Max Verstappen in first practice at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was fifth fastest, but did not get a lap on the fastest soft-compound tyres after stopping on track with a hydraulic leak.

Russell, who trails Antonelli by 81 points, was 0.4 seconds quicker than Verstappen.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were third and fourth, both just over 0.4secs off Russell's pace and right behind Verstappen.

But neither Italian car ran the soft tyre as the teams completed varied programmes to start off the weekend in Baku.

Antonelli, who ended up 0.878secs off Russell's fastest time, was the fastest driver in the early running using the hard tyres.

The Italian stopped at Turn One on his first lap on the soft tyres, with smoke seeping out of the cooling vents on his engine cover.

He missed half the session so will have some catching up to do in the second session later in the day.

Live commentary on BBC Radio 5 Live and Sports Extra; live text updates on BBC Sport website and app

Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad were seventh and eighth, ahead of Haas driver Esteban Ocon, who is fighting for his F1 career after admitting on Thursday that he is a free agent for 2027.

The Audis of Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hulkenberg, which both have a major upgrade, were ninth and 10th.

Hulkenberg stopped on track with a technical problem towards the end of the session, shortly after Lindblad had made an error at Turn Seven and stopped facing the barriers. The British rookie was able to reverse out and get going again.

Russell and Verstappen were other drivers to make an error, both taking to the run-off area when they missed their braking points, the Mercedes driver at Turn Three and Verstappen at Turn One.

articles.title: Sainz da un buen salto y Alonso no sale del fondo... y penalizado
articles.standfirst: Las mejoras parecen haber impulsado a Williams, mientras la rebaja de peso en el Aston Martin no se notan de momento
articles.summary: Las mejoras parecen haber impulsado a Williams, mientras la rebaja de peso en el Aston Martin no se notan de momento
articles.body: George Russell, ante la ausencia de Antonelli más de media sesión, ha conseguido el mejor tiempo en los libres 1 del GP de Azerbaiyán, por delante de Max Verstappen y los Ferrari de Leclerc y Hamilton. Las diferencias son mínimas, apenas 0,4 segundos en un circuito muy largo, por lo que la llegada de Kimi y de los McLaren, que estuvieron probando el medio coche nuevo con el que han llegado a Bakú, augura un fin de semana lleno de batallas en una de las pistas más divertidas del calendario de F1. Los españoles llegaban con mejoras en ambos coches, rebaja de peso para Alonso en el Aston y de peso y aerodinámica en el Williams para Carlos. La impresión fue dispar para ambos. En el lado de Sainz parece que ha sido positivo el nuevo chasis aligerado en el FW-48, además de cinco grandes modificaciones aerodinámicas. De estar cerca de los últimos Madrid, sube al 12º, seguido por Albon en el 13º, unos puestos que los de Grove no conocían desde la primavera, pues ambos están a unas dos décimas de la Q3. Y todo ello pese a un problema inicial en los frenos traseros, que se le tostaron después de 5 vueltas iniciales. La preparación fue muy rápida en el box del '55'. En el caso de Alonso, acabó 19º, superando sólo a Stroll y Bottas de entre sus rivales naturales y con algunos pasajes raros, como una pasada de frenada en la cueva 1 con el segundo juego de gomas (medios), a la que siguió un golpeo del volante y soltarse de manos un rato después, como si algo estuviera fuera de funcionamiento por completo. Hay que esperar, pero los 22 km/h de velocidad punta menos que el Mercedes de Russell parecen indicar dónde sigue el problema, que es en la falta de potencia de la unidad Honda. Fernando, como Stroll, cambiará varios elementos del motor para la calificación y la carrera en Bakú, el ICE (unidad interna de combustión) y el turbo, lo que obligará al asturiano y a su compañero a penalizar y salir la parte final de la parrilla (o el pir lane) este domingo. Antonelli, nada más colocar el neumático blando, sufrió una avería en el sistema hidráulico, lo que le obligó a detener el coche y bajarse cuando quedaba más de media hora para el final de la sesión. No es una pérdida vital, pero empieza con un pequeño contratiempo el fin de semana en una pista que le va como anillo al dedo a su estilo. Ha ganado en Miami, en Mónaco, en Madring y le tocaría Bakú, de entre los circuitos urbanos o híbridos para hacer un pleno descomunal. Kimi empezó donde lo dejó, primero después de la primera tanda en Bakú con el neumático duro, pero con Max Verstappen muy cerca y eso que el de Red Bull levantó el pie en casi toda la recta trasera de su mejor giro. Fernando Alonso subía al 11º con ese compuesto de la banda blanca, aunque con tres rivales sin tiempo por problemas y parecía experimentar un pequeño salto respecto a Madring. Sainz, por su parte, cerraba la tabla de tiempos por una avería en los frenos traseros, por la que sólo pudo rodar 5 vueltas. Albon era 14º con todas las novedades del Williams y el chasis aligerado. Tiempos, cortesía de formula-timer.com.

articles.title: Flavio Briatore se cansa de 'abuso argentino' contra Gasly, por parte de los fans de Colapinto
articles.standfirst: Avisa de que podría no dejar a Franco con los medios de sui país si sigue la campaña contra el francés
articles.summary: Avisa de que podría no dejar a Franco con los medios de sui país si sigue la campaña contra el francés
articles.body: Un momento de la carrera de Madring, en el que Pierre Gasly llevaba un neumático más lento por delante de Franco Colapinto, y Alpine no le indicó al francés que se apartara antes de entrar en boxes, ha provocado una situación prolongada de dos semanas de insultos y amenazas en redes por parte de los fanáticos del piloto argentino hacia el grancés. Y eso ha arrastrado hasta Bakú dos semanas más tarde. El asesor ejecutivo de Alpine, Flavio Briatore, ha amenazado con un bloqueo informativo en los medios argentinos respecto a Colapinto, tras los insultos que sus fans han proferido contra su compañero. Pierre Gasly ya dijo este miércoles que, "mi familia y yo hemos recibido insultos inquietantes", refiriéndose a la reacción por parte de los 'hooligans' de Franco tras lo sucedido en Madrid. "Personalmente, me parece un poco preocupante para nuestro deporte", añadía el primer piloto de la escuadra francesa. “Soy un atleta de élite, así que sé que estoy expuesto; siempre ha sido así. Pero la magnitud de las amenazas y los ataques me parece completamente inapropiada, especialmente cuando van dirigidos a familiares, a mi novia, etc”, añadía. Por su parte, Briatore ha criticado duramente la situación y ha declarado en ESPN (la cadena que tiene los derechos de la F1 en Argentina) que impedirá que Colapinto hable con los medios argentinos "si sus aficionados no le apoyan de la manera correcta". “Sobre todo para los argentinos, porque no se trata de los italianos ni nada por el estilo”, dijo refiriéndose a la descrita reacción de los aficionados cuando se le preguntó sobre el incidente entre Colapinto y Gasly. No es la primera vez que se produce esta situación respecto a Colapinto, como otros incidentes, como la sanción recibida en Holanda que provocó una reacción fuera de lugar de unos de sus patrocinadores o los insultos proferidos a Ollie Bearman tras un choque con el de Alpine. La FIA ya ha avisado que no permitiría el abuso 'on line' de ninguna forma y su presidente, Mohammed Ben Sulayem ha advertido personalmente que tomarán medidas severas contra este tipo de comportamientos.

images.caption: Briatore, en el 'paddock' de Bakú este jueves. REV RACING PRESS

articles.title: Lindblad, del muro de Madring... al de Bakú
articles.standfirst: El británico provocó la primera bandera roja del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán con un golpe en la difícil zona del Castillo
articles.summary: El británico provocó la primera bandera roja del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán con un golpe en la difícil zona del Castillo
articles.body: Arvid Lindblad suma 31 puntos en su primera temporada en la Fórmula 1 y con sólo 19 años, es el más joven de la parrilla superando a Kimi Antonelli, ya ha empezado a generar argumentos a su favor para ser considerado un candidato a nombre importante de futuro. Más si cabe en el mundo salvaje de Red Bull y su exigente filial Racing Bulls. Pero los fallos siguen existiendo, y en el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán volvió a golpear en un muro, algo que también vivió en la anterior cita, la de Madring. Es un accidente parecido en su contexto. En Madrid se veía a un buen Lindblad, pero cerró el viernes perdiendo el control del RB tras una compresión después de La Monumental. El caso de Azerbaiyán se asemeja porque su coche está en el top-10, es candidato a Q3 con los Alpine o Audi, y su día de libres vuelve al muro. El chico de origen indio sufrió un golpe habitual en Bakú. En el exigente sector intermedio cayó en la subida al Castillo, una zona en la que, por ejemplo, Leclerc se ha estrellado en un par de ocasiones. Lindblad quiso ajustarse al lateral, pero impactó y el problema llegó al quedarse enganchado su tren trasero que volvió a dar con el muro. La suspensión quedó reventada. El choque de Lindblad no fue el único incidente de la segunda sesión de libres. Poco después de darse el semáforo verde tras el golpe del RB, otro piloto británico tuvo que abandonar la sesión. "Mi motor se ha roto", lanzó Ollie Bearman a través de la radio. La unidad de potencia en el Haas se apagó cuando se disponía a tirar... y corre riesgo de tener que cambiar los componentes para el viernes y sábado. Y tampoco escapó de las dudas Aston Martin. Alonso vivió como su mejor vuelta del día era cortada por el golpe de Lindblad y al regresar a boxes se vio a los mecánicos de Honda trabajando en la zona del motor del AMR26. No pudo regresar a pista al mismo tiempo que sus rivales.

images.caption: Lindblad, con su RB totalmente roto. CAPTURA TV
Bearman, parado. CAPTURA TV

articles.title: Formula 1 teams expect final call on Qatar, Abu Dhabi Grands Prix by middle of October on closing 2026 season races
articles.summary: Haas' Ayao Komatsu and Audi's Mattia Binotto say teams told earlier this week that they would know by mid-October whether the season-ending Middle East races go ahead; watch final practice in Baku on Friday at 9.30am, with Qualifying at 1pm, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
​The 2026's season is due to finish with a back-to-back races in Qatar (November 27-29) and Abu Dhabi (December 4-6) but those events have appeared uncertain for a number of months owing to the conflict this year in the Middle East, which started in February.

The two events remain on the calendar, which currently runs to 23 races, with Sky Sports News understanding that the intention is for them to take place.

Italy's Imola circuit is thought to be the contingency option to close the season if it is deemed that the Middle Eastern rounds cannot go ahead, with F1 having more time before a final decision is made.

An F1 Commission meeting took pace on Monday and, speaking in Thursday's press conference at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, team chiefs said they had been given clarity on when a decision would be taken by.

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said: "I believe that Stefano [Domenicali, F1's president] is targeting to tell us in mid-October so we all know what the situation is.

"I believe that Imola is getting ready in case we have to do it [there].

"But hopefully things can stay as a baseline and we can go to Qatar and Abu Dhabi. That'd be really good."

Audi counterpart Mattia Binotto added: "We discussed it during the F1 Commission last Monday. Mid-October is the last call for such a decision."

What's the latest on Qatar and Abu Dhabi GPs?

Sky Sports' F1 correspondent Craig Slater:

"The latest information I have from leadership sources at Formula 1 itself is that they are both on the calendar, the intention is to go.

"I have been informed that, as things stand in terms of the level of stability in the region, should those events have been happening in the next couple of weeks, it would be stable enough for them to go ahead. The situation would be that unless there is a deterioration again then those races would be going ahead.

"There is a contingency of Imola but they do not have to commit to that to the exclusion of those last two races. So Imola will be a contingency situation if they can't run the last two races, but they will compensate Imola for any financial loss they make in getting ready for that. "

"Mid-October is the teams' understanding that they will get some kind of clarification on that matter, so we will have to watch this space to a degree.

'I do hope that we get to go there' - Hamilton keen on Middle East return

Speaking in Baku on Wednesday, Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton said he hoped the sport was able to return to the Middle East as scheduled at the end of November

"I personally want to go. I love going to the Middle East," said Hamilton.

"From what I've read, I think things seem OK out there. But I don't have all the information so I don't know what the risk levels are. But I trust in Stefano to make the right decision for the sport, but I do hope that we get to go there.

"Finishing in winter in Imola might not be the best weather-wise, and also it's a beautiful track, but it's not a track that we're going to be doing any overtaking in and the more races, the better."

articles.title: Una fuga de aceite noquea a Alonso
articles.standfirst: El asturiano no pudo completar una vuelta rápida al 100% en los libres tras otro problema en el motor Honda
articles.summary: El asturiano no pudo completar una vuelta rápida al 100% en los libres tras otro problema en el motor Honda
articles.body: Parece una pesadilla que no termina y no cesará hasta dentro de unos tres meses. La temporada 2026 de Fernando Alonso, como ya fueron las de 2015, 2016 y 2017 en su segunda etapa con McLaren, estará marcada por su relación tormentosa con Honda. Llegó al Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán con la noticia de una penalización de 25 puestos (al fondo de la parrilla) al cambiar la parte de combustión de su unidad de potencia y en pista siguen los problemas. Para variar... El asturiano no pasó de las ocho vueltas en la segunda sesión de libres en Bakú tras otro problema en la unidad de potencia. El de Aston buscaba su vuelta rápida con el compuesto blando, pero el parón tras el accidente y bandera roja de Lindblad precipitó los acontecimientos. Al entrar en boxes empezaron a trabajar en su coche... y ya no salió más. Las imágenes no llevaban a equívocos. Los mecánicos de Honda ponían atención en el motor porque se reportaba una fuga de aceite. Era el 'KO' en toda regla para el jueves, sin posibilidad de llegar a tiempo para completar alguna vuelta más. Otro problema más a una lista interminable que va desde las vibraciones de inicio de año, la manejabilidad con la evolución presentada en Holanda, batería... Los datos tampoco son especialmente alentadores. El Gran Premio parece uno de prueba y test, pero los progresos no se ven a simple vista. Del jueves salió a 4.542 del mejor tiempo de Russell (1:43.347) y la barrera de los cuatro segundos parece como el primer listón a evitar como ejemplifica el mejor Aston del día, el de Lance Stroll (puesto 21º a +4.056). No son los 5.4 de Spa, pero siguen las dudas. Y la Q1 es una condena insalvable. Eso sí, el bicampeón asturiano mantiene su fe en encontrar el camino. "No tengo dudas, al 100% se arreglará todo", ha repetido durante toda la temporada. Los datos dolorosos siguen en las velocidades punta. En el punto de detección, Alonso marcó una punta de 311 km/h. Muy lejos de los 338 km/h del mejor registro de Hadjar con su unidad de potencia Red Bull Power Trains - Ford. Y lo que es más preocupante, pues hasta los F2 (Mini marcó 328 km/h en su práctica) alcanzan mayor punta. Cabe esperar cierto subidón con un motor fresco en el viernes y sábado, pero la situación sigue siendo dramática.

images.caption: Alonso se baja del Aston Martin. CAPTURA DAZNF1
Alonso, con su Aston Martin en los libres. LAPRESSE
Los mecánicos de Aston Martin en el coche de Alonso. LAT Images

articles.title: Mercedes se destaca, en un duro golpe de realidad para Sainz y Alonso
articles.standfirst: Russell por delante de Antonelli, que estuvo media hora parado. Lo de Williams y Aston no se explica, con Checo 13º
articles.summary: Russell por delante de Antonelli, que estuvo media hora parado. Lo de Williams y Aston no se explica, con Checo 13º
articles.body: Las carreras pasan y Mercedes sigue imperturbable en la cabeza de la tabla de tiempos. Esta vez fue Russell, por delante de Antonelli, el que se llevó el mejor crono, aunque beneficiado por el hecho de que el italiano se perdiese media hora por la mañana y media por la tarde, debido a una avería en el sistema hidráulico de su W17. Max Verstappen empezó muy bien la sesión con los blandos, atisbando la posibilidad de un fin de semana en el que pueda romper la sequía de triunfos que le persigue esta temporada, pero la diferencia final de 0,8 segundos respecto al primero de los Mercedes hacen pensar que le será muy complicado en Azerbaiyán. Los Ferrari están a más de un segundo y los McLaren, escondidos como todos los viernes, pero con posibilidades de regresar a la pole, como en Madring hace dos semanas. Ese es el dibujo por la zona cabecera tras el jueves. Y por la parte trasera, de nuevo aparecen los españoles. Alonso, con avería, terminó 22º y último, como antes de las mejoras de chasis y de motor en el parón del verano. Williams ha mejorado, pero el salto que se intuía por la mañana queda en agua de borrajas tras el FP2, con Carlos Sainz en el puesto 17º. Inapreciable casi. A falta de de 24 minutos para el final y tras 8 vueltas con el compuesto blando, Fernando tuvo que bajarse del coche, después de que los operarios de Honda se acercaran para levantar la cubierta por algún problema. Aston Martin había anunciado el cambio de media unidad de potencia para este fin de semana, pero eso suele hacerse el sábado (en este caso el viernes), es decir para calificación. Pero en este caso, Honda confirmó por la tarde que se trataba de la nueva, por lo que habrá que colocar otra segunda a estrenar para el resto del fin de semana. Los japoneses rizando el rizo. Es de esperar que la nueva unidad de combustión interna, el turbo y los escapes le de algo más al '14' el resto del fin de semana, que ha empezado realmente torcido para él. En el caso de Williams, la bajada de 12 kilos y el aumento de puntos de carga en su FW48 apenas se refleja en ganancia. La Q3 estaría a 0,8 segundos, en lugar del 1,5 de antes de las evoluciones de este fin de semana, pero llegar a los puntos sigue siendo una quimera. Viendo el 13º final de Checo Pérez con el Cadillac, cabe preguntarse como un equipo nuevo en todo y el más modesto de la parrilla ha mejorado más puestos esta año que un imperio como Aston Martin, que se ha gastado en una fábrica nueva y fichajes técnicos de tronío más de 2.000 millones en tres años. Williams también ha invertido mucho en estos dos años tras la llegada de Sainz y de Vowles, pero parecen estar más perdidos que nunca. En su caso, con un motoraco de Mercedes bajo el capó, es todavía más sangrante en cuanto a posibilidades mecánicas. Bakú parece de nuevo una tortura, como las anteriores, para los nuestros. Arvid Lindblad se estrelló a falta de 40 minutos en la zona del castillo, perdiendo el RB y rompiendo la suspensión trasera derecha, algo que interrumpió de golpe la sesión y dejó poco tiempo para probar los ritmos de carrera. Afortunadamente, no fue nada serio para el piloto británico. El holandés seguía muy entonado con el RB22, que estrena pontones rediseñados en Bakú y parece acercarse a ese gran objetivo de ganar su primera carrera en 2026, algo que tiene entre ceja y ceja y que será complicado que no consiga en lo que resta. articles.title: Horarios de los Libres 3 y la Clasificación del GP de Azerbaiyán en Bakú y dónde ver en TV los entrenamientos de Alonso y Sainz
articles.standfirst: El Mundial se va acabando y aún quedan muchos asuntos que cerrar
articles.summary: El Mundial se va acabando y aún quedan muchos asuntos que cerrar
articles.body: Regresa la acción a la F1 en las calles de Bakú, con el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán, el cual, esta temporada, se adelanta una jornada debido a una fiesta nacional en el país europeo. Con un Mundial cada vez más sentenciado a favor del joven Kimi Antonelli, las 9 carreras restantes, contando Azerbaiyán y a la espera de ver qué sucede finalmente con Qatar y Abu Dhabi, estando Ímola como posible recambio, nos vaticina un final de temporada bastante abrupto en cuanto a carreras se refiere. Tras las dos últimas victorias del piloto de Mercedes, en Monza y Madring, a Antonelli se le empieza a poner muy de cara el Título Mundial de Pilotos, batiendo además un récord de precocidad, al conseguirlo con apenas 20 años recién cumplidos y el cual actualmente lo posee, ni más ni menos que el cuatro veces Campeón de F1, Sebastian Vettel, quien lo consiguió con 23 años y 154 días. Aún y así, ante tal magnitud de su objetivo, Kimi parece no achantarse ni sucumbir ante la presión, al mantener la cabeza fría y la meta de frente: continuar en la dirección que llevan siguiendo durante toda la temporada sin malgastar ningún punto. Además de que el nivel de Kimi está siendo claramente superior esta temporada, sus principales rivales a disputarle el Mundial son incapaces siquiera de plantarle cara o ponerle un poco más difícil el camino al claro candidato al Título. Por un lado tenemos a George Russell, compañero de Kimi y segundo en la general, quien ve cada vez más lejanas sus opciones en el Mundial y ha empezado a desasirse de la idea de lucharle el Mundial a Antonelli. A un total de 81 puntos, a falta aún por disputarse 225 puntos, teniendo en cuenta todas las carreras, Russell ve el nivel de su compañero muy superior al del resto de contrincantes y claramente inalcanzable. Otro de los pilotos que parecían poder plantare cara era Lewis Hamilton. Tras finalmente haberle pillado el punto a su Ferrari gracias al cambio de reglamento, el 7 veces Campeón del Mundo tenía la potestad de iniciar una guerra Alumno vs. Maestro hasta Madring, donde un DNF le llevó a abrir una brecha de 191 puntos contra Kimi. Un cambio de reglamento que podría haber sido favorable para los españoles ha resultado ser un completo desastre. El Aston Martin de Alonso y el Williams de Sainz han desaprovechado por completo la oportunidad de mejorar lo que llevaban años implantando y hacer así un coche competitivo. Ante esta situación, Alonso y Sainz tratan de dar el máximo posible cada fin de semana, con el único fin de encontrar puntos fuertes que les puedan servir de cara a la próxima temporada. Sainz contará con un coche 'completamente nuevo' a partir de este fin de semana, tal y como ya aseguró su Jefe de Equipo, James Vowels, mientras que Alonso sigue sin dar señales claras sobre su futuro, manteniendo así a todo el mundo a la espera y en vilo de ver si el asturiano continuará en el Mundial a partir de la próxima temporada o, por el contrario, cerrará definitivamente una su etapa en la F1. Isack Hadjar, finalmente recuperado de su lesión en la muñeca izquierda y tras haberse perdido los últimos tres Grandes Premios, se subirá de nuevo a su Red Bull este jueves en Bakú, haciendo que, a su vez, Lawson regrese a su puesto en Racing Bulls y Tsunoda al de sustituto. Como es habitual, el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán de Fórmula 1 2026 se podrá ver en directo por televisión a través de DAZN F1 y en Movistar +. También tienes la opción de seguir todo lo que suceda en la carrera en el circuito de Bakú a través de los directos de MARCA.com y la transmisión de la carrera en Radio MARCA. articles.title: Jamie Chadwick tests F1 car for first time with Williams run in Portugal in 'best day of my life so far'
articles.summary: Triple W Series champion and Sky Sports F1 pundit completed 32 laps in Williams' 2025 car in the Algarve; first woman to drive Williams car since 2015; watch the full story of Jamie Chadwick's Williams test across Sky Sports F1's Azerbaijan GP shows on Friday and Saturday
articles.body:
The Williams ambassador and Sky Sports F1 pundit, who races in the European Le Mans Series, completed 32 laps in their podium-finishing 2025 car at the circuit in the Algarve under F1's Testing of Previous Cars (TPC) rules on Monday.

British 28-year-old Chadwick is the second woman to test an F1 car this year after reigning F1 Academy champion Doriane Pin drove a 2021 Mercedes at Silverstone in April, and the first British female to do so since Jessica Hawkins ran an Aston Martin in 2023.

Chadwick, who first joined Williams in 2019 as a development driver, has enjoyed a successful career in motorsport so far, winning all three seasons of the all-female W Series and, in 2024, becoming the first woman to win a road course race in the US-based Indy NXT series.

"It was a phenomenal day and an incredible experience," said Chadwick.

"Few things can prepare you for driving a Formula 1 car at speed around a track like Portimao, but it was everything I imagined and 10 times more.

"I'm incredibly grateful to Atlassian Williams F1 Team for this opportunity. I remember being young and watching Susie Wolff step into a Williams F1 car and how much that inspired my own journey.

"I'd love to be able to do the same for the next generation, and the experience I gained today will make a real difference both to my own racing and to what I can pass on to the drivers coming through.

"I'm so grateful and incredibly happy with how the day went. It's an experience I'll remember for a very long time - I'd go as far as saying it's been the best day of my life so far."

Susie Wolff is the last woman to drive in Friday practice in F1, completing in four sessions across the 2014 and 2015 seasons for Williams, while Italian Lella Lombardi in 1976 was the last woman to start a Grand Prix.

Williams team principal James Vowles said: "Jamie Chadwick is an inspiration for millions of women and girls who has broken records at every level, and she has thoroughly earned this F1 test opportunity with Atlassian Williams F1 Team.

"Jamie gathered important data for the team as F1 prepares to return to Portimao next year, and her feedback and performance were impressive as we knew they would be.

"This clearly shows there is a path for women to compete at the top level, and I look forward to seeing how Jamie uses this experience to advance her own driving and advise our young drivers on what it takes to drive an F1 car."

Speaking to Sky Sports before heading to Portugal, Chadwick detailed how her preparations for the test had gone.

"I did half a day in the sim, the seat fit and all the kind of procedural stuff that you do beforehand," she said. "And then I have actually been upping the neck training a lot.

"Obviously racing LMP2, I train my neck anyway, but that is naturally stepped up for an F1 test.

"George Russell's been helping me a little bit with the preparation. I woke up the next morning after the first proper day of neck training I did with him, and I could barely move my head!

"So it's incredible, actually, when you realise what they are going through in terms of not just in the car, but also the training that they have to do for the necks at the moment. It's crazy."

Chadwick had previously driven the Portimao track in European Le Mans, and added: "I've spoken to quite a few drivers about it.

"Ollie Bearman said mentally it's one of the toughest tracks, actually. Just this flow of it is very undulating. There's a lot going on. In the mind it's very busy.

"I feel like I learn a huge amount from Formula 1 just generally in the role that I have with Sky Sports, which has helped me a lot in all the other stuff that I'm doing.

"But I think this is going to take a new, extreme one from that."

articles.title: Azerbaijan GP: George Russell fastest in second practice ahead of Kimi Antonelli in dominant start in Baku
articles.summary: Mercedes make a commanding start to the Azerbaijan weekend, with George Russell in early flying form; Red Bull's Max Verstappen only driver within one second of Mercedes' pace; watch final practice in Baku on Friday at 9.30am, with Qualifying at 1pm, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
​​Mercedes' Russell built on the form that had seen him top the day's earlier first practice session to stay at the head of the timesheet, this time finishing with a half-second advantage around the challenging streets of Baku.

Antonelli, who leads Russell by 81 points in the chase for 2026's Drivers' Championship, experienced a compromised Thursday owing to the hydraulic leak that stopped his car midway through the opening session.

The Italian returned to the track with just over 30 minutes of the second session left, after an engine change, and worked his way up to second on the timesheet, eventually finishing 0.552s behind Russell.

"We lost quite a few laps in FP1 and missing half of FP2 is never ideal, especially on a street circuit," said Antonelli.

"Overall, I feel like it was a good recovery. I feel quite good in the car. A few things to work on but looking forward to tomorrow."

Max Verstappen took third to end a promising opening day in an upgraded Red Bull car, although his deficit to the front was 0.8s.

Everyone else was over a second off the pace, including the Ferraris and McLarens. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were fourth and fifth respectively, with McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri sixth and eighth.

Norris described McLaren's deficit to the front as "pretty pants".

Pierre Gasly was seventh for Alpine with the returning Isack Hadjar ninth for Red Bull and Esteban Ocon, whose Haas seat appears set to go elsewhere for 2027, 10th quickest.

Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad brought out Thursday's only red flag when he crashed in the narrow castle section of the challenging Baku lap.

Is Baku poised to be Russell vs Antonelli?

After falling in excess of three race wins behind Antonelli last time out in Madrid, Russell admitted he was not in a realistic fight for the championship despite being his team-mate's nearest challenger in the points.

Russell, though, said on Wednesday that he felt he was in the form to win races again - something he has not done since the Austrian Grand Prix in June - and he has certainly made a positive start to that quest in Baku, where has finished on the podium in three of the past four years.

"He's driving well," said Sky Sports F1 's Jacques Villeneuve after the second session.

"Where he makes the difference is all the narrow bits where the car needs to be precise. Antonelli drives with more understeer, so pays a bit of a price there.

"It seems like a straight fight between the two [Mercedes] team-mates."

articles.title: Sainz: "El coche se nota más rápido... pero venimos de tan atrás"
articles.standfirst: El español cree que para ver paso más grandes, "habrá que esperar ya al año que viene"
articles.summary: El español cree que para ver paso más grandes, "habrá que esperar ya al año que viene"
articles.body: Carlos Sainz, tras el 17º puesto en los libres 2 de Baku, afirma que Williams ha mejorado aunque eso aún no se refleje en las posiciones de la clasificación. Sus primeras sensaciones eran positivas, pese a que él mismo lleva tres meses diciendo que no se podía esperar un milagro de la evolución introducida este fin de semana. "La sensación inicial es que definitivamente el coche se nota un poco más rápido... pero estábamos tan atrás que, aunque hayamos traído una mejora importante, seguimos teniendo mucho terreno que recuperar", valoraba el '55' en F1 TV. "Tal y como se esperaba, no ha habido sorpresas enormes en cuanto a ritmo. Es un paso adelante positivo, pero si queremos dar pasos más grandes, tendremos que esperar al año que viene", subrayaba Carlos, para indicar que en 2026 no hay mucho más que rascar. Un gran resultado para carlso el resto del fin de semana sería, "quizás intentar pasar a la Q2 con algo más de facilidad y ver si podemos luchar contra algunos rivales en esa fase. Pero será difícil; venimos de unas carreras en las que a veces estábamos incluso por detrás de los Aston Martin. Así que dar un gran paso adelante ya supondría estar luchando por entrar en la Q2", planteaba. En cuanto a los frenos ardiendo en los libres 1, el piloto de Williams, autor de un podio en esta pista en 2025, explicaba: "Sí, en realidad todo surgió de un fallo en la radio. Se desconectó y, cuando entré en boxes, el equipo no estaba preparado porque no teníamos comunicación por radio". "Por eso se incendiaron los frenos. Fue una combinación de un problema operativo y un fallo de fiabilidad que nos hizo perder tiempo en pista tanto en los libres 1 como en los 2, lo cual no es lo ideal en un circuito como este. Pero bueno, en las pocas vueltas que pude dar en ambas sesiones, sentí que habíamos dado un paso adelante y que podemos ser más competitivos que en los fines de semana anteriores", cerraba.

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Sun Goddess to scoop big Cheveley Park Stakes prize at Newmarket
articles.summary: Despite still recovering from injury, Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle will have a keen eye on Newmarket as the Cheveley Park Stakes looms this weekend; Speaking to Simon Mapletoft, Hollie took time to preview the pick of some top-class action from Headquarters.
articles.body:
New York to gain reward in Friday highlight

I'm looking forward to a great weekend of action at Newmarket, including the mouthwatering Group 2 Betway Joel Stakes (3.00) - for me the highlight of an exciting card on Friday.

Godolphin's 116-rated colt Talk Of New York is the one I believe they all have to beat following his eyecatching run at the Qatar Goodwood Festival when he made up a lot of ground to be second in the Group 3 Thoroughbred Stakes.

Before that he got within two lengths of the brilliant Bow Echo in the St James's Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot and can gain his reward at the probable expense of the ever-reliable Persica - such a solid horse who has done nothing wrong this year.

He had Hankelow behind in a Group 3 at Haydock Park last time and can confirm that form with Karl Burke's colt, who hasn't hit the heights expected of him this year but showed a glimmer that day and should appreciate a sounder surface.

The Group 2 Betway Rockfel Stakes (2.25) on Friday can go to Wathnan Racing's Goodwood winner Light Of Dawn who relished the step up to this seven furlongs when taking the Group 3 Prestige Stakes so emphatically.

Karl Burke's filly steps up in grade but has hopefully taken another step forward since we last saw her and can get the better of Eve Johnson Houghton's Sugar Yes Please - another filly I admire.

She also won a Group 3 over seven furlongs, taking the Sweet Solera on Newmarket's July Course, while Ed Walker's Siena Storm could have more to offer after finishing three lengths behind Light Of Dawn in the Prestige.

Class dropper tough to beat in Princess Royal

Inis Mor has been keeping some pretty hot company this season and can enjoy the spotlight in the Princess Royal Stakes (1.50) on Friday.

David Menuisier's filly has been placed in both the French and Irish Oaks since scoring at Listed level and has been found a great opportunity to win in Group 3 company with Ryan Moore on top and a 7lb weight for age allowance in her favour.

Coedana has made strong progress this season and showed her potential behind subsequent Irish Champion Stakes hero Hotazhell and close second Wimbledon Hawkeye in a Group 1 in Germany. That's solid form and this big, galloping track will play to her strengths.

The race of the day at Newmarket on Saturday is the Group 1 Tattersalls Sceptre Sessions Cheveley Park Stakes (2.27). The fillies' showpiece pitches Aidan O'Brien's prolific Sun Goddess against runaway Prix Morny winner Senorita Bonita and Albany heroine Libertango.

Sun Goddess was behind Libertango in the Albany but has since gone on to win two Group 1s as well as the valuable Sales race at York's Ebor Festival and sets the standard for me.

George Boughey's filly found Senorita Bonita too good in the Duchess Of Cambridge Stakes at Newmarket so there's not a great deal between the principals, but I do think Aidan's filly can edge it.

At a bigger price, I'd love to see Andrew Balsing's Moonrise get into the act. I've followed this tough filly closely this summer and expect her to pay the form of her Group 3 win on Polytrack a huge compliment.

Clive Cox's concerns about testing ground in France were vindicated when his Norfolk Stakes star Orthodox lost his unbeaten record in the Group 1 Prix Morny last month and he can prove that run all wrong in the Tattersalls Middle Park Stakes (3.00) on Saturday.

That said, it's going to take a big performance to put a dent in the flawless record of Godolphin's Inner City Blues , who has been kept under wraps since taking the Group 2 July Stakes at Newmarket.

The Dewhurst entry gets my vote just ahead of Orthodox while Aidan O'Brien's Marco Polo is a fascinating runner after putting his Gimcrack disappointment behind him in a Curragh maiden. Aidan wouldn't be pitching him in at this level if he didn't think he had the class to go well.

The Tattersalls Online Royal Lodge Stakes (1.55) on Saturday is a strong renewal, with Aidan O'Brien's proven Group winner Haffner stepping up to 1m for the first time. The Acomb hero is better than he showed in testing ground last time in the National Stakes and is a threat to all.

However, I like the progressive profile of Charlie Appleby's Godolphin colt First Law who won his maiden at Sandown before seamlessly stepping into Listed company at Haydock Park at the beginning of the month.

Karl Burke's Burning Up is also unbeaten in two starts and has a similar profile but has a bit more to prove at this stage so I'm pinning my hopes on First Law staking his Classic claims under William Buick at a track where the Appleby team excels.

There's a big handicap in Hand Of God who can come good in the £200,000 bet365 Cambridgeshire (3.40) at Newmarket on Saturday. Harry Charlton's five-year-old confirmed the promise of his Newbury win in the spring with a huge second in the John Smith's Cup at York when he didn't get the rub of the green.

He can be forgiven his defeat in Group company in France lasty time and looks better value than likely favourite Gavriel, whose Ascot win for Team Gosden has been franked. Though penalised for that, he's progressive and should be in the mix.

I'd like to see Alan King's Alcarath go well at bigger odds with conditions in his favour. He's been running well without winning and remains well handicapped off a mark of 92, particularly if the first-time cheek pieces give him an edge.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.

articles.title: Azerbaijan GP: Lando Norris rules McLaren out of Baku pole fight as George Russell expects margins to 'tighten' in qualifying
articles.summary: Mercedes dominated Thursday's practice sessions at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix while McLaren were over one second off, leaving Lando Norris downbeat; watch final practice in Baku on Friday at 9.30am, with Qualifying at 1pm, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Norris was 1.5 seconds slower than pace-setter George Russell in second practice with the slow-speed 90-degree corners seemingly not suiting McLaren's car.

McLaren have brought a major upgrade package to the car in Baku, including new sidepods, engine cover, diffuser and floor edge but the new parts have not instantly given them more performance.

"We are miles off. We are up there relative and in the position we expect to be in but we are 1.5 seconds off the pace. Pretty pants," said Norris, who is 106 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli with nine rounds to go.

Asked if McLaren can close their practice deficit to Mercedes, he added: "I hope so. I have no idea. We will see what work we can do tonight. The car doesn't feel that bad, so it's a little knife in the heart when you see how far off you are.

"I just care about the pace and we are not very fast. I drive whatever car I get given. I just want it to be quick and it's not very quick at the moment."

Norris aborted a lap in second practice which likely would have put him at least within one second of Russell, who topped both practice sessions on Thursday.

McLaren chief technical officer Rob Marshall says it's "early days" with the eight new items on the car and everything is working as expected.

"We had a lot of new bits on the car - a lot of learning. You put your package on and you need to learn how to dial it in and I don't think we are there yet," he said.

"I think the car is doing what we want it to do. The aero maps seem pretty happy. It's just a matter of dialling the performance in."

Russell: I'm sure the gaps will tighten in qualifying

Qualifying takes place on Friday at 1pm with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix itself on Saturday at 12pm, all live on Sky Sports F1 , as Sunday is Remembrance Day in Azerbaijan.

Although you can overtake in Baku, track position is still important because it's a street circuit and Russell says "there's still plenty of work" to do for Mercedes.

"It's been a positive first day here in Baku. The car felt competitive over a single lap, and our race pace looks closely matched with McLaren and Red Bull," he said.

"I'm sure those gaps will tighten even further when we get to qualifying tomorrow."

Kimi Antonelli suffered a hydraulics leak in first practice, then Mercedes were forced to change his engine ahead of second practice which cost him one hour of running in total.

But, the championship leader, who is 81 points ahead of Russell, was still in second in second practice and half a second off his team-mate.

"We tried to do the maximum with what we had. We lost quite a few laps in FP1 and missing half of FP2 is never ideal, especially on a street circuit," said Antonelli.

"Overall, I feel like it was a good recovery. I feel quite good in the car. A few things to work on but looking forward to tomorrow."

Max Verstappen was Mercedes' closest challenger in the two practice sessions but still over eight tenths off the pace at the end of the day, despite Red Bull bringing upgrades to Baku.

Isack Hadjar was back in the car for the first time since the end of July after missing the last three race weekends due to a wrist injury he suffered in last month's summer break.

Hadjar, who has been confirmed to remain as Verstappen's team-mate in 2027, also lost valuable track time due to an engine problem in first practice but was still "pretty happy".

"It feels good. I had a good feeling. Not many laps unfortunately but this will come. I'm not really worried too much about the pace," he said.

"The feeling with this new package, we know the characteristics are the same with the car, but it feels nice - better than when I left it in Budapest."

Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were in the top five of both sessions but the seven-time world champion feels Ferrari are missing performance on the tyres and on the straights.

"I felt generally good in the car. The track is awesome to drive. FP1 I felt very strong and I thought we were doing well but in FP2 the others took another step," said Hamilton, who has avoided a penalty for allegedly impeding Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson in second practice.

"It's trying to understand, we didn't change anything on the car, but the others took a step somehow. These tyres are really, really difficult to get to work. You do an out lap and a prep lap and they are still not in the window and still don't provide you with the grip.

"When you do an extra lap, all of a sudden they switch up and you have tonnes more grip, so that's a really fine line and really difficult to get working. But we try our best and some teams do it better than others. We have to look into that.

"Then our straight line speed is not as good as Mercedes. Whether we can close that deficit tomorrow, we will try to work on tonight. Otherwise, a fun day."

Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur added: "The sessions were difficult to read. For sure, each parameter of performance - fuel, engine made a bigger difference compared to a normal track.

"They [the drivers] were not very pleased with the balance so we have a lot to do tonight to find a good solution for tomorrow.

articles.title: NASCAR Hall of Famer Darrell Waltrip steps back from public life for serious health concerns
articles.summary: Darrell Waltrip, who parlayed a Hall of Fame driving career in NASCAR into a long-time broadcasting stint at Fox Sports, has stepped away from public life due to a progressive brain disease.
articles.body: FRANKLIN, Tenn. — Darrell Waltrip, who parlayed a Hall of Fame driving career in NASCAR into a long-time broadcasting stint at Fox Sports, has stepped away from public life due to a progressive brain disease. Waltrip and his family shared a statement on Wednesday that noted the former driver, “has been diagnosed with Frontotemporal Degeneration (FTD) complicated by possible Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy (CTE) — likely from injuries incurred during his racing career.” The 79-year-old Waltrip was one of NASCAR’s storied characters, one of the first to build a brand around his supersized personality, and he served for decades as one of the sport’s strongest ambassadors. Waltrip won 84 races and Cup Series championships in 1981, 1982 and 1985 before moving straight into the broadcast booth. He was inducted into the third class of the NASCAR Hall of Fame in January 2012. Waltrip was Fox Sports’ first hire when the network launched its NASCAR coverage in 2001 and became widely known for his signature “Boogity! Boogity! Boogity! Let’s go racing, boys” call. A fearless Kentucky boy who first showed up on the NASCAR scene in 1972 at Talladega Superspeedway in Alabama, Waltrip aggravated his competitors by beating them on the track and then running his mouth out of the car. Rivals nicknamed him “Jaws” and Waltrip was at the forefront of parlaying his personality and fame into a lucrative side hustle of appearances, celebrity endorsing and, finally, the broadcast booth. “While this disease will inevitably progress, thankfully it is currently limited to some minor noticeable symptoms,” the family said in a statement. “As a result, he will be stepping further away from the public limelight. Be assured, Darrell is happy and otherwise healthy — spending his time with his wife, Stevie, two daughters and his three young grandchildren. We are all grateful for your continued prayer, love and support! Boogity! Boogity! Boogity!”

images.caption: Darrell Waltrip on May 21, 2023, in North Wilkesboro, N.C.

articles.title: Team principal: Audi F1 retain Hülkenberg and Bortoleto for 2027
articles.summary: Nico Hülkenberg will continue to drive for Audi in the 2027 Formula One season during which the German will turn 40. Team principal Mattia Binotto said at th...
articles.body:
Nico Hülkenberg will continue to drive for Audi in the 2027 Formula One season during which the German will turn 40.

Team principal Mattia Binotto said at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on Thursday that the works team will also continue with their young Brazilian driver Gabriel Bortoleto.

Binotto said that both had contracts for 2027, "so we knew there would be no change. We thus never announced what it would look like next year because there was no necessity for it."

Hülkenberg joined F1 in 2010 and Audi, formerly Sauber, in 2025. Bortoleto, 22, joined the same year. Audi is in its first season as a works team after a full takeover of Sauber.

Hülkenberg claimed his first career podium in his 239th race by coming third at last year's British GP.

Binotto said that the German is very consistent and rarely makes mistakes: "He always gets the most out of the car and scores points whenever possible. He has performed well so far."

Audi are eighth from 11 teams in this season's constructors' standings with 17 points, of which Bortoleto has garnered 10 and Hülkenberg seven.

articles.title: Dale Earnhardt once broke his hand punching a man who killed a deer on his North Carolina farm
articles.summary: Dale Earnhardt Jr. recounts the wild story of his dad tackling and punching a trespasser who snuck onto his North Carolina farm to shoot a deer.
articles.body: Dale Earnhardt wasn't called "The Intimidator" for nothing. But as it turns out, the seven-time NASCAR Cup Series champion didn't reserve all that intimidation for the racetrack. Just ask the guy who decided to sneak onto his property and shoot one of his deer. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS During Wednesday's episode of "The Dale Jr. Download," Dale Earnhardt Jr. recalled the time his dad broke his hand punching a man who killed a deer on his North Carolina farm. And while Earnhardt Sr. certainly wasn't afraid of a confrontation on the track, his son said he couldn't recall his dad ever getting into an actual fight with another driver. The deer incident, though… that was a different story. Dale Earnhardt didn't take kindly to trespassers According to Dale Jr., the whole thing started back in 1993 when a man working on a tractor on Earnhardt's property spotted some deer. Later that afternoon, the man went to a bar with a buddy and started telling him about the animals he'd seen. And, as tends to happen when alcohol enters the equation, the two came up with a brilliant idea. They'd sneak back onto Earnhardt's property and shoot themselves a deer. "The more they drank, the braver they got," Earnhardt Jr. recalled. So, around dark, the two men hopped the fence and made their way onto the property. What they didn't know was that Earnhardt and his farm manager happened to be walking along a power line nearby. The two heard a gunshot and watched as a wounded deer ran down the clearing before collapsing. Rather than immediately confronting the trespassers, Earnhardt and his farm manager hid in the tree line and waited for the men to come retrieve the animal. CHASE BRISCOE SAYS DEER HUNTING GIVES HIM A BIGGER RUSH THAN DRIVING 200MPH IN NASCAR And when they showed up, The Intimidator lived up to his nickname. According to Dale Jr., his dad charged the man carrying the gun, tackled him and began punching him in the face. He hit the guy so hard that he broke his own hand. Earnhardt eventually recognized the man's voice and realized he was the same guy who had been working on his tractor earlier that day. He then held the man until police arrived. Talk about a bad day at work. The Intimidator had a soft spot for his deer Earnhardt wasn't upset because someone had stolen a deer he was planning to hunt himself. He just liked having the animals around. According to his son, Earnhardt had some impressive bucks roaming his property, but he wasn't interested in shooting them. He enjoyed watching them and wanted to keep them around. And he certainly didn't want word getting out that his farm was home to some big deer. So when Earnhardt showed up to the 1993 NASCAR awards banquet sporting a cast on his broken hand, he made up a different explanation for the injury. "He didn't want people to know about his deer," Dale Jr. explained. "He didn't want more people showin' up, trying to sneak into his property." Earnhardt even had a black-and-white cast to match his tuxedo as he accepted his sixth Cup Series championship trophy. But the broken hand created another problem when the 1994 racing season rolled around. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER According to Junior, his dad was told he wouldn't be allowed to compete in the Daytona 500 while wearing the cast. So Earnhardt cut it off himself. Problem solved. Anyway, let that be a lesson to you. Don't go hunting on private land without permission. It just doesn't turn out well — not for you, not for the deer, and not even for the landowner who has to knock your lights out. Love all things hunting, wildlife and outdoors? articles.title: Darrell Waltrip’s NASCAR Career: Championships, Wins and Greatest Moments
articles.summary: From three Cup championships and 84 victories to a long second career with FOX Sports, Darrell Waltrip left his mark on nearly every corner of NASCAR.
articles.body:
Darrell Waltrip spent nearly five decades making his mark on NASCAR, first from behind the wheel and later from the broadcast booth.

Now, renewed attention is on the NASCAR Hall of Famer following difficult news about his health. Waltrip and his family announced in September 2026 that he has been diagnosed with frontotemporal degeneration, complicated by possible chronic traumatic encephalopathy, and will step further away from public life.

The news has prompted another look at just how much Waltrip accomplished during one of the most decorated and distinctive careers in NASCAR history .

Waltrip won 84 NASCAR Cup Series races, captured three championships and eventually conquered the Daytona 500. He became virtually unbeatable at Bristol Motor Speedway for a stretch and, after retiring from driving, became one of NASCAR's most recognizable voices on television.

Here are some of the moments and numbers that defined his remarkable career.

Darrell Waltrip Won 84 NASCAR Cup Series Races

Waltrip made 809 Cup Series starts between 1972 and 2000 and won 84 of them.

Those 84 victories still rank fifth in NASCAR Cup Series history, behind only Richard Petty (200), David Pearson (105), Jeff Gordon (93) and Bobby Allison (85). Waltrip had long shared fourth place with Allison before NASCAR officially recognized Allison's disputed 1971 Bowman Gray victory as his 85th career win in 2024.

Waltrip's first victory came at Nashville in 1975. His final win came 17 years later at Darlington Raceway in 1992.

The stretch in between included one of the most dominant periods NASCAR has seen.

Waltrip won 12 races in 1981 and did it again in 1982. Those back-to-back monster seasons also produced back-to-back Cup championships.

He finished his career with 59 poles, another mark that places him fifth in Cup Series history.

Three NASCAR Championships Defined Waltrip's Prime

Waltrip won the Cup Series championship in 1981, 1982 and 1985, all while driving for legendary team owner Junior Johnson.

His first two title seasons showcased Waltrip at his most dominant. He won 24 races across 1981 and 1982 alone.

The third championship came differently. Waltrip won three times in 1985 but used remarkable consistency, including 21 top-10 finishes in 28 starts, to claim another title.

It was an era in which Waltrip wasn't simply winning. His personality made him one of the sport's central characters.

He was outspoken, confident and sometimes polarizing. The nickname "Jaws" followed him after rival Cale Yarborough compared the talkative Waltrip to the shark from the blockbuster movie.

Bristol Motor Speedway Became Darrell Waltrip's Playground

If one track best illustrates just how dominant Waltrip could be, it's Bristol.

Waltrip won 12 Cup races at Bristol Motor Speedway, still the most in track history.

Even that number doesn't fully capture what he did there.

From 1981 through 1984, Waltrip won seven consecutive Cup races at Bristol. For more than three years, NASCAR's best drivers showed up to one of its most demanding short tracks and nobody beat him.

Waltrip eventually added a 12th Bristol victory in 1992, the same season he earned the final Cup win of his career at Darlington.

He was similarly formidable at North Wilkesboro Speedway, where he won 10 times.

Waltrip Finally Won the Daytona 500 in 1989

By 1989, Waltrip had already won three championships and dozens of Cup races.

But he still hadn't won NASCAR's biggest race.

In his 17th attempt at the Daytona 500, Waltrip stretched his fuel over the closing laps and drove the No. 17 Hendrick Motorsports Chevrolet to one of the most significant victories of his career.

Then came a celebration almost as memorable as the win itself.

Waltrip performed his version of the "Ickey Shuffle" in Victory Lane and spiked his helmet, creating an enduring Daytona 500 moment.

It would be his only victory in the Great American Race.

Waltrip Built an Entire Second NASCAR Career With FOX

Waltrip's final Cup Series start came in 2000, but his relationship with NASCAR was far from over.

He joined FOX Sports for its inaugural NASCAR Cup Series season in 2001 and spent 19 seasons in the broadcast booth.

His first Daytona 500 broadcast became an unforgettable and ultimately heartbreaking day. Waltrip watched his younger brother, Michael, earn his first Cup victory while Dale Earnhardt was involved in the last-lap crash that claimed his life.

Over the next two decades, Waltrip became as familiar to a younger generation of fans behind a microphone as he had been behind the wheel.

His signature "Boogity, boogity, boogity" call became part of FOX's NASCAR broadcasts before Waltrip retired from the booth in 2019.

Darrell Waltrip's NASCAR Career by the Numbers

Cup Series championships: 3 (1981, 1982, 1985)

Those numbers alone put Waltrip among NASCAR's greatest drivers.

But they don't entirely explain his place in the sport.

Waltrip could win races, irritate rivals, entertain a crowd and command a television broadcast. NASCAR named him one of its 50 Greatest Drivers in 1998 and included him again when it expanded the list to 75 drivers for its 75th anniversary in 2023.

For fans who watched him race, he was one of the defining drivers of his era. For those who came later, his voice became part of Sunday afternoons.

Few people have been part of NASCAR for as long, or left their fingerprints on as many different parts of it, as Darrell Waltrip.
